memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "He then presented the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head. Then Moses slaughtered the ram and splashed the blood against the sides of the altar. He cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces and the fat." - Lev 8:18-20 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The sin offering dealt with guilt. Now comes the burnt offering — the one where everything ascends, nothing held back.

The order is instructive. Cleansing, then consecration. Forgiveness, then full surrender.

We sometimes get this backwards and demand that people surrender their whole lives before we assure them they are forgiven. That is a heavy burden to place on anyone, and it is not God's sequence. The bull came before the ram.

But note that the ram did come. Forgiveness was not the end of the ordination; it was the doorway into total dedication.

There is a version of Christianity that stops at the sin offering — grateful for forgiveness, uninterested in surrender. Leviticus 8 will not allow that. Aaron's hands went on both animals.

Paul makes the same movement in Romans. Eleven chapters explaining God's mercy, and then: Therefore, I urge you, brothers and sisters, in view of God's mercy, to offer your bodies as a living sacrifice (Rom 12:1). In view of mercy. Surrender is the response to grace, never the price of it.

You have been forgiven. Now, what are you holding back?

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have I received forgiveness without ever moving on to surrender?
2. What part of my life have I never placed on the altar?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You for forgiving me completely. In view of that mercy, I offer You the parts of my life I have kept back. Amen.
